strengths: Every world setting has a lifetime: the three lists at scripts/settings.mjs:1162-1194 tag all 71 world registrations and nothing else (scripted 20.11.2026), so a season setting the reset forgets is a tagged absence, not a silent one (tier 0 R1256 holds them; its result not read).

Every world setting that promises a redraw has one: the 22 keys handed to onWorldChange (settings.mjs:3463-3465) are exactly the 22 rows of sync.mjs SETTING_KINDS, and the GM stores' keys go through onStoreChange with a named kind (3473-3475), so R171's rule about raw store keys is kept in the file that registers them.

The boot cannot be taken down by one subsystem: every registration in module.mjs is under `safely` (152-158), the relay guard and the GM chrome run before the requirements check, and a stopped module takes its stylesheets off the page (module.mjs:187-191, requirements.mjs:157-186).

The migration stamp is held back on three separate grounds - a failed clause (with a permanent notice), a clause that answered notPrimary, and a primacy lost at either end of the pass (migrate.mjs:1696-1729) - and every lift reads back before it removes and throws when its secret stayed (578-599).

The automatic road of the safeword clause now asks the world whether it was played (worldWasInPlay, read before anything writes at ready: migrate.mjs:1549-1573, 1756-1762); a new world is no longer given the old word (the old CORE-13 on that road).

The settings windows write only what differs and through game.settings.set, so each setting's onChange runs once, a reload is asked once with Foundry's own question, and a world row is drawn and written only for a user Foundry lets modify settings (settings-window.mjs:123-130, 402-439).

Death and the incident's seats are each one pure table in the leaf (settings.mjs:3647-3670, 3794-3865), with the readers' rules written beside them; the Eclipse count adds what is in flight so two fast drags cannot both read the old count (3925-3971).

Daggerheart's character settings window is dressed, never rebuilt: hidden fields stay in the form with their values, the words are replaced after every render, and each field gets a name a screen reader reads (dh-settings.mjs:29-34, 111-130, 175-211).

findings.title: The repair the GM handbook names, game.drpg.migrate({ force: true }), sets a default world's safeword to MISIUBOMBO and tells the GMs the world already had it; it also gives back a bedroom stash a GM removed
findings.where: scripts/migrate.mjs:1659 and 1671 (force skips the `since` gate; wasInPlay becomes Boolean(from)); 1579-1614 (keepOldSafeword); 1019-1039 (bedroomStashes); docs/handbooks/gm-handbook.en.md:1897; lang/en.json and lang/pl.json DRPG.Legacy.safeword
findings.what_happens: A forced pass re-enters every clause regardless of the stamp. keepOldSafeword's only guard against a world that never used the old word is `if (!from && !wasInPlay) return null`; on a stamped world `from` is set, so a world whose safeword is still the default "Safe Word" - every world created on 1.2.x whose GM never typed one - is written the language file's legacy word MISIUBOMBO, and the GMs are whispered DRPG.Safeword.kept: 'This world already has the safeword "MISIUBOMBO", so that word stays.' The same pass runs bedroomStashes, whose own note says a sweep would put back a stash the GM removed on purpose (TRAP 76) and that the clause is gated to run once for that reason; forced, it gives every Bedroom owner without a stash an open one again. The handbook offers the forced pass as the safe repair ('Running it twice changes nothing the second time').
findings.failure_scenario: A GM whose world misbehaves runs game.drpg.migrate({ force: true }) as the handbook says; every player's Safeword button now reads MISIUBOMBO, a word the table never agreed, and the GM's card says the world already had it.
findings.expected: A forced pass repairs without re-seeding: the safeword clause keeps the default on a world stamped after 1.1.39 (the clause's own `since`), and a seeding clause stays gated by its stamp even when forced (migrate.mjs:90-101 says the gate is what tells a seed from a GM's removal).
findings.refutation_tried: Followed game.drpg.migrate to migrate1_2_0 with the options passed through (api.mjs:735). Looked for another guard in keepOldSafeword: only `from`/`wasInPlay` and the current value against DEFAULT_SAFEWORD. The legacy key is MISIUBOMBO in both language files, so a Polish GM gets the same. The tier-2 test 'an unstamped world in play keeps its safeword' (tests-tier2.mjs:56560) drives only from: "", and tier 1's line 7002 reads the guard's text; neither drives a stamped world. Checked the other seeding clauses: openStudentSheets raises default ownership to OBSERVER, which anonymity.mjs holds anyway (776-835), so it is harmless; unseedMessengerChime removes only the seeded path and says so (133-138). A downgrade was also considered (the stamp is written whatever the direction): back to a build at or above 1.2.113 it re-runs nothing, so it is not written as a finding.
findings.tests_near: tier 2 'an unstamped world in play keeps its safeword' (scripts/tests-tier2.mjs:56560); tier 1 source check at scripts/tests-tier1.mjs:7002; result of neither read (no base-run.json).

findings.title: Game settings never redraws while open, and its Save writes back every row that differs from the stored value - so a change another GM saved meanwhile is undone
findings.what_happens: The window is drawn once from the settings as they stood at open. saveSettings walks every row and writes each field whose value differs from the setting's value now - not each field the user touched. A world row that another GM (or an Assistant) changed and saved while this window stood open still shows the old value, differs from the stored one, and is written back on this GM's Save, with its onChange (and, for a requiresReload row such as the dice look or Voice in Foundry's window, the reload question for every client). Nothing redraws the open window on updateSetting, against the owner's standing rule that a window redraws at once when what it shows changes.
findings.failure_scenario: GM A opens Game settings to change Crossing rooms costs a Move; GM B meanwhile switches Lock players' resources off and saves; A presses Save and the lock is on again for the whole table, with neither GM told.
findings.expected: A row the user did not touch is not written (compare with the value the window was drawn with), and the window follows updateSetting for the rows it shows, as keepLive does for the module's other windows.
findings.refutation_tried: The header says the window writes 'as Foundry's form did' (settings-window.mjs:37-45; v13's SettingsConfig #onSubmit read as text, v14's shape LIVE-E49-02): Foundry's own form has the same compare-with-now shape, so this is a copied behaviour, but no paper records accepting the lost update or the stale window for the module's own window. Looked for a refresh: no keepLive, no updateSetting or clientSettingChanged listener in settings-window.mjs or look.mjs. Looked for other writers of the rows so a single GM could meet it: of the window's 25 world rows only documentLanguage has another writer (i18n.mjs:147, the first start's seed), so the case needs two users who may modify settings, which the module supports (Assistant GMs, a second GM). The client window has the same shape, but no other road writes its rows (grep), so it is not written as a finding.
findings.tests_near: R3420 holds the sections; the tests that call saveSettings (five test files name it) were not read for this case; none found that saves over a value changed after the window opened.

findings.title: Three older clauses answer null when their read-back fails, so the runner counts them as 'nothing to do' and stamps the world, against the file's own rule to throw
findings.what_happens: Each of these reads back after its write, and on a mismatch logs an error and returns null. migrate1_2_0 treats null as a clause with nothing to do (1682), so no clause is listed as failed and the stamp is written; the clause is `since`-gated and never runs again on that world. The header says a clause that could not finish what it is for throws, so the world is not stamped and the next load tries again, and the lifts below follow it.
findings.failure_scenario: On a world whose motive write did not land, the GM sees no failure notice and the motive stays without a timer, read as already due, for good.
findings.expected: Throw where the read-back fails, as the lifts do (578-599).
findings.refutation_tried: Checked the runner: only a throw reaches report.failed (1687-1693). The clauses are old (1.1.37-1.1.43) and only a world stamped before them reaches them, and a failed world-setting write is rare, which is why this is a nit.
findings.tests_near: none found that plants a failed read-back for these three.

findings.title: Document language offers 'Not set yet' as a choice a GM can save, which empties the world's language until the next primary start
findings.where: scripts/settings.mjs:1733-1744 (choices include ""), scripts/settings-window.mjs:96 and 389-390 (the select writes it), scripts/i18n.mjs:144-148, scripts/utils.mjs:167-176
findings.what_happens: The select in Game settings > gm lists 'Not set yet' beside English and Polski, and fieldValue accepts "" because it is a key of the choices. Saved, the setting is empty: worldLocalize then writes each document in the page language of whichever browser writes it - the mixed-language log D196 exists to stop - until the primary GM's next ready seeds it again with that GM's language.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM unsure which language to pick leaves 'Not set yet' selected and saves; cards a Polish player's browser writes come out in Polish and the English GM's in English, in one log.
findings.expected: 'Not set yet' shown only while the setting is empty, and not offered once a language is written.
findings.refutation_tried: The empty choice is deliberate so that the default is among the choices (settings.mjs:1739-1741, E66 fix r1 F12, R1164); that note is about Foundry's default check, not about a GM saving it. No guard in saveSettings or fieldValue refuses "".
